text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Foreign trade surplus from January to October 1996 reaches 103 billion francs.
-- Culture Minister Philippe Douste-Blazy says SFP TV/film production company to be privatised in mid-1997.
-- October foreign trade surplus is 16.93 billion francs.
-- GEC Alsthom wins 700 million franc contract for 18 passenger railway cars to Portugal.
-- Small business minister Jean-Pierre Raffarin predicts robust Christmas season, but first figures show consumption is down over November.
-- Government to sell SFP to Generale des Eaux and Havas after 1.2 billion franc cash injection.
-- Aerospatiale likely to build missiles with Diehl, not Dasa.
-- Courts to rule on British Airways takeover of Air Liberte on January 8.
-- French government announces receipt of letter from Algeria's Armed Islamic Group threatening more violence in France.
-- France rejects pact for new American-led air patrols in Iraqi airspace.
